note: Databricks Feature Store manages governed features for training and serving with point-in-time correctness.
Feature tables store reusable features as Delta tables with primary key constraints and UC governance.
Feature Views declaratively define features with automatic materialization in batch, streaming, or hybrid modes.
On-demand features compute Python UDFs at request time with UC governance for integrated serving.
Point-in-time joins construct training datasets with historical feature values to prevent train-serving skew.
Online Feature Store provides sub-millisecond latency lookups via managed PostgreSQL with read replicas and automatic offline sync.
Feature serving endpoints provide REST access with Model Serving integration for dynamic feature lookup.
Feature discovery enables tagging, cross-workspace search, and Catalog Explorer integration.
Feature lineage automatically captures feature tables and models used in training with governance via Unity Catalog.
Lineage visualization shows data flowing through features and models to serving in Catalog Explorer.
Databricks Operate provides production monitoring, quality evaluation, and CI/CD automation for continuous improvement.
Inference Tables capture AI Gateway request and response payloads to Unity Catalog Delta tables for quality analysis.
Data Profiling automatically calculates quality metrics with baseline and window comparisons for drift detection.
Snapshot profiles capture a single point-in-time baseline of table metrics for anomaly detection.
Timeseries profiles track metric evolution across time windows for trend detection and anomaly comparison.
Inference profiles monitor prediction payload distribution and output characteristics over time.
Drift Detection runs statistical tests on predictions and features to identify distribution shifts against baseline or recent windows.
Numeric drift tests include Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Wasserstein distance, and Population Stability Index for distributions.
Categorical drift tests include chi-square, total variation distance, and Jensen-Shannon divergence for distributions.
Custom Metrics define aggregate, derived, and drift metrics with layered recomputation to minimize overhead.
Aggregate metrics are direct computations from table columns like count, mean, and standard deviation for reuse.
Derived metrics compute domain-specific KPIs and quality indicators from aggregate metrics using SQL.
Drift metrics compare current window metrics against baseline to detect statistical shifts.
Monitoring auto-generates quality dashboards with alert configuration for drift detection.
Lakeview dashboards visualize profile metrics and drift results with pre-built templates and custom parameterization.
SQL alerts trigger on metric thresholds or anomaly detection with configurable refresh intervals.
Notification channels support email, webhook, and Slack with PagerDuty for on-call escalation.
MLflow Evaluation provides built-in LLM judges for GenAI correctness and relevance with custom scorers reusable across environments.
Production Monitoring runs evaluation scorers on sampled traffic, collects human feedback, and combines results with dashboards.
MLOps Stacks provides reference templates combining ML code, bundle configuration, and CI/CD workflows for GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps.
Declarative Automation Bundles define ML infrastructure as code in YAML for reproducible deployments across environments.
Jobs resources define Lakeflow Jobs with triggers, tasks, and dependencies for orchestrated workflows.
Pipelines resources define Lakeflow Pipelines with SQL and Python for declarative ETL with quality expectations.
Models resources define registry entries and manage versioning with stage promotion workflows.
Experiments resources configure MLflow experiments in bundles for workspace organization.
Endpoints resources define model serving endpoints with scaling, traffic splitting, and feature integration.
Permissions resources define fine-grained access control with roles for all bundle resources.
Lakeflow Jobs provides DAG-based orchestration with serverless execution up to 1000 tasks and repair run support.
Job Triggers enable automated execution via cron schedules, table events, or API calls.
Cron schedule triggers execute jobs based on cron expressions with UTC or workspace timezone support.
Delta table triggers initiate job runs on table commit detection for data-arrival workflows.
File arrival triggers initiate jobs on cloud storage path events with wildcard pattern support.
Model registry event triggers automate deployment pipelines on production transitions or version registration.
Continuous loop triggers run jobs repeatedly with minimal latency between completions.
API-triggered runs enable manual job execution with dynamic parameter passing via REST or UI.
Lakeflow Pipelines provides declarative ETL with SQL and Python, auto-scaling, and data quality expectations.
SQL declarative mode uses native DLT syntax for tables and views with automatic dependency inference.
Python declarative mode uses decorators for tables and views with complex imperative logic in pipelines.
Quality expectations policies define row handling (warn, drop, or fail) on constraint violations.
Git Integration provides native version control with multi-branch support, conflict resolution, and CI/CD automation.
